--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_prefix_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the prefix tree (trie) of a list of paths. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_prefix_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the prefix tree (trie) of a list of paths. title: >- [Graph.add_prefix_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add the prefix tree (trie) of a list of paths. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add the prefix tree (trie) of a list of paths. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15696-L15794){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_prefix_tree( paths, source_attr="source", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Prefix tree](../assets/graphs/add-prefix-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three prefix trees (tries), each node labeled with the character it stands for and hung from an unlabeled root at the top. Paths that share a prefix share its nodes, so ab and ac branch below a single a, and every path ends at the one NIL node at the bottom, as in NetworkX." width="100%"} Each path is a sequence of items, such as the letters of a word. The prefix tree has a root, one node for each distinct prefix of the paths, and a shared NIL node marking the end of a path: walking from the root, each step adds the next item, and paths that start the same way share their first nodes. Each node stores the item it adds in the `source_attr=` node attribute; the NIL node stores `"NIL"` and the root nothing. A path that ends at a node (because it is complete there) joins that node to NIL, so the paths can be read back as the root-to-NIL walks. Nodes are created as in NetworkX's `prefix_tree()`: the root first, then NIL, then the prefixes depth first, each node's children in order of first appearance. NetworkX numbers the root `0` and NIL `-1`; here they are simply the first two new nodes. Edges run from each prefix to its extensions (and to NIL), which a directed graph keeps as their direction. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Prefix trees are useful for: - storing and searching a set of words or sequences by prefix (autocomplete, spell checking, routing tables) - comparing sequences, such as event logs or clickstreams, by their shared beginnings - building directed trees from lists of root-to-leaf paths ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [paths]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The paths, each an iterable of hashable items (a string is a path of characters). [source_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["source"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's item. Default is `"source"`, as in NetworkX. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a path is not iterable or holds an unhashable item. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four words share their first letters. The tree has a root, NIL, and one node per distinct prefix: ::: {#c3ea8127 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_prefix_tree(["ant", "and", "bee", "be"]) tree.count_nodes(), tree.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (9, 11) ``` ::: ::: Each node keeps the letter it adds. `"1"` is the root and `"2"` the NIL node: ::: {#f92b5171 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree.get_node_df().select("label", "source") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Every word is a walk from the root to NIL, and "be" ends at the node that "bee" passes through: ::: {#a32b8d75 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['1->3', '3->4', '4->5', '5->2', '4->6', '6->2', '1->7', '7->8', '8->2', '8->9', '9->2'] ``` ::: :::
